92	### Phase 2: automated actions on a delivered server (same branch)
93	
94	Nxeon owns the machine upstream and keeps out-of-band control; the customer gets root inside the OS only (their own SSH key; nothing Nxeon-owned is installed in their OS). The customer never sees the supplier.
95	
96	**Rule: nothing mutates from the web tier.** Customer/admin actions (`lib/actions-dedicated-ops.ts`, `lib/actions-dedicated-ops-admin.ts`) only validate and insert a `DedicatedJob`. The worker sweep `dedicated-jobs` (`worker/dedicated-jobs.ts`, every 10 s) is the only place an upstream write happens: it runs `lib/dedicated/ops.ts` `runJobStep` and, for the real upstream, sends every write through `lib/ovh-admin/write.ts` `ovhAdminWrite` (rights check, per-actor and per-target rate limits, AuditLog before and after). Every job end also writes a `DedicatedServerEvent` and an AuditLog row; a failure notifies every ADMIN.
97	
98	**Modes.**
99	- `dedicated_ovh_dry_run` (Setting, **default `"true"`**): nothing is sent; jobs finish "Dry run: ...". The admin server page shows a DRY RUN / LIVE badge. Set `"false"` to go live.
100	- `NXEON_DEDICATED_OVH_MOCK=1` (ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`): a fake upstream (`lib/dedicated/ovh-mock.ts`, file-backed so web + worker share it) for demos; the customer panel shows a "Demo machine" badge.
101	
102	**Safety.** The target is always `DedicatedServer.providerServiceName` from OUR row (customers pass only our server id). A service name equal to any `Node.providerServerId` (or listed in Setting `dedicated_ovh_protected_services`) is refused before any call, so a mistyped link can never touch a platform node. rDNS / firewall IPs must lie inside the blocks upstream reports for that service. Disruptive actions (reboot, rescue, reinstall, handover): one at a time per server, 6 per hour per server; 30 actions per hour per customer; typed confirmation (the server's name) for reinstall; blocked while impersonating.
103	
104	**What the customer can do** (`components/dedicated/DedicatedControlPanel.tsx`, on `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]` once the server is ACTIVE and linked):
105	- Overview: power, boot mode, network port and traffic, detected hardware (GETs, cached 20 s).
106	- Hard reboot (`POST /dedicated/server/{sn}/reboot`, task polled). No soft reboot exists upstream; the panel says to use `sudo reboot` for a graceful restart.
107	- Rescue: netboot rescue with the customer's SSH key (`PUT /dedicated/server/{sn}` `{bootId, rescueSshKey}` + reboot), back to disk the same way. If staff ever get a rescue password, they store it encrypted on the admin page (`rescueSecretEnc`) and the customer reveals it (`decryptSecret`).
108	- Reinstall: images from `GET .../install/compatibleTemplates`, filtered and renamed (`lib/dedicated/ops-core.ts` `offerableTemplates`: no Windows/licensed, panel, BYOI or "withapp" images), hostname + one of the customer's SSH keys, typed confirmation, `POST .../reinstall` `{operatingSystem, customizations:{hostname, sshKey}}`, progress from `.../install/status` + the task. Nxeon adds no deploy key (the VPS flow injects only the customer's keys too).
109	- Reverse DNS (`POST /ip/{block}/reverse`), network firewall per IPv4: on/off, add/remove rules (`/ip/{block}/firewall/...`, validated by the existing `lib/ovh-admin/validate.ts` rules).
110	- Extra IPv4 (1, 4 or 8): priced from `dedicated_ip_price_cents`, prorated to the next renewal (`extraIpProrateCents`), paid wallet-then-card (Stripe metadata `nxeonDedicatedIpOrder`, fulfil branch `dedicatedIpOrder`). Lands as `DedicatedIpOrder` PAID. **Nothing is bought until an ADMIN clicks "Approve purchase"** on the server page; approval enqueues `IP_ORDER`, which creates an upstream cart, adds the IP product for that size routed to the server (`destination`, `country`), checks out with the account's payment method, waits for delivery, then adds the block to the server and the monthly price to `renewalMonthlyCents` (+ `extraIpMonthlyCents`). "Reject & refund" returns the full charge to the wallet.
111	- Remote console: **not shipped to customers.** The upstream only offers its own hosted KVM/SOL pages (`/features/ipmi/access`), so the panel offers "Open a ticket" and staff open the console.
112	
113	**Handover (auto-install).** On a PENDING/PROVISIONING server, after staff buy the machine and save its service name, "Install & hand over" (admin server page) enqueues `HANDOVER`: install the OS the customer ordered (matched by label) with the customer's first SSH key, then mark ACTIVE, fill IPs from upstream, set hostname/OS, notify in-app and send the `dedicated_server_ready` email template (`prisma/seed-email-templates.ts`; never sent in mock mode). A customer with no SSH key: the button refuses; deliver credentials by hand.

158	**Tags** (`lib/dedicated/tags.ts`, pure, `test/dedicated-tags.test.ts`), computed once over the in-stock catalogue: **Most popular** = admin pin (`DedicatedCatalogItem.popularPinned`, checkbox on the catalogue item page) else the build with the most paid orders in 180 days if ≥ 3; **Recommended** (only when neither exists, never labelled "popular") = cheapest in-stock NX-Forge with ≥ 64 GB; **Best value** = lowest 10% price per (cores + RAM GB/8); **High performance** = top 10% by threads × boost clock; **GPU**; **New** = first seen in the last 30 days and ≥ 7 days after the first sync. 161	
162	**Icons.** `bmrack`, `bmblade`, `bmchip`, `bmgpu`, `bmstack` in `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` (violet tone, so bare metal never reads as a blue VPS mark); service mark `public/nx/svc/baremetal.svg` and card plate `public/nx/preview/baremetal.svg` (`SvcIcon name="baremetal"`).

164	**No custom builds.** Every "Ask for a custom build" / "Request this build" / "source a specific machine" CTA was removed (portal, legacy marketing page, NXM page, FAQ now says unlisted hardware can't be ordered).
165

# Brief: bm-ops (bare metal backend, admin, policy, health)
Read `/root/agent-notes/bm-release/CONTEXT.md` first. Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/bm-ops -b feature/bm-ops main`. Notes to `/root/agent-notes/bm-release/ops/`.

Do an honest end-to-end audit AND fix what you find. Answer each owner question with evidence (a table in your report: question, answer, how you verified, status).

1. **Auto deployment and auto pay.** Trace order to delivery: quote, wallet or card payment, our order record, the supplier order, payment capture ordering (never order before paid; never lose money paid for an order that fails; idempotency on retries and double-clicks), provisioning polling, OS install, delivery, credentials/IP reaching the customer, and renewal (auto-pay from wallet then card, failure handling, grace, suspension, termination). Exercise every branch against the mock and Stripe test mode with tests (extend `test/dedicated-order*.test.ts`). Find and fix bugs (partial failure, stuck orders, stale quotes, price drift between quote and charge, stock disappearing mid-checkout).
2. **IP purchases.** How does buying extra IPs work end to end (the IP order flow, `DedicatedIp`/`DedicatedIpOrder`, pricing, assignment to the server, reverse DNS, firewall/virtual MAC if applicable)? Does it work in the mock? Is it equivalent to what the supplier's own panel can do (list the panel's IP features vs ours and mark gaps)? Fix gaps that are in scope; list the rest.
3. **Parity with using the supplier panel.** Compare what a customer can do in our dashboard (power/reboot, rescue, reinstall, IPs, rDNS, monitoring, network, KVM/IPMI, backups/storage, boot options, DDoS settings) with the supplier's panel capabilities; produce a gap table with severity; implement the safest high-value gaps if small, otherwise write them up.
4. **No refunds, no discounts for dedicated servers (hard business rule).** Enforce it in CODE, not just copy: (a) no coupon, promo, partner/creator sitewide discount, referral credit, first-month-free, grandfather price, term discount or any other price reduction may apply to a dedicated order or renewal (find every discount mechanism with `grep` and prove each is excluded, with tests); (b) no refund path may touch a dedicated order: block customer-facing "money-back" copy and flows (check `MoneyBackNote` and any "30-day guarantee" text on dedicated surfaces), block admin refund tools on dedicated invoices/orders with a clear message (admin can still correct billing errors through an explicit, audited, separate mechanism: propose it, do not widen refunds), cancellation means the server runs to the end of the paid period with no proration or refund, and chargeback handling is documented. Add an explicit non-refundable acknowledgement requirement to the order (`acceptedNoRefundAt` recorded on the order; the wizard agent shows the checkbox, you enforce it server-side). Update ToS/terms text that is in the repo. Flag (do not decide): whether signup wallet credit / promo wallet credit may pay for a dedicated server (it is a discount in effect) and recommend.
5. **Admin portal management.** Review `app/admin/dedicated/*`: what can staff do today (see orders, servers, stock/catalogue sync, pricing rules, pin popular builds, regions, per-server actions)? Build what is missing for safe operation: an orders queue with states and stuck-order alerts, per-server detail with the supplier references (admin-only, names the supplier is fine), manual actions that are audited (retry a failed provisioning step, refresh server state from the supplier, mark delivered, send credentials again), renewal/billing view, health panel (catalogue sync age, mock/live flag, failed jobs), and an audit log. Everything role-gated like the other admin areas.
6. **Caching: customers must never wait on a supplier API call to render their dashboard.** Audit every customer-facing read path: the server dashboard, My Services rows, power state, IP lists, network, metrics. They must render from our DB/cache instantly, refreshed by worker jobs and by explicit refresh actions with sensible TTLs, with a visible "last updated" and graceful behaviour when the supplier is slow or down (stale data shown, never a spinner-forever or 500). Fix any path that calls the supplier during page render; add a cache layer where missing (DB-backed snapshot with `fetchedAt`, per-server refresh job, single-flight so concurrent viewers trigger one refresh). Measure render time with the supplier mock made artificially slow (e.g. 8 s) and show before/after.
7. **Health before public release.** Produce `/root/agent-notes/bm-release/ops/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`: every function that must be verified on a real server before the public flag is flipped (a short list the owner can run), plus monitoring and alerting gaps (failed jobs, stuck orders, supplier errors, price/stock sync failures) and what you fixed. Do NOT flip any public flag.
8. **Tracking data for the wizard agent.** Ensure the order/server record exposes what the wizard's tracking needs without a supplier call at render: status, step, `orderedAt`, expected delivery window (derive from the catalogue's stock/availability code such as 1H/24H/72H and from actual historical order-to-delivery durations in `DedicatedServer` once enough data exists), datacenter label (customer-facing name, never the supplier's), and the supplier task state when available (cached). Coordinate through `lib/dedicated/tracking.ts` types: read the wizard agent's branch `feature/bm-wizard` if it has committed them; otherwise define `lib/dedicated/tracking-data.ts` for your side and note it.

Tests, `devhost tsc` clean, screenshots of the admin screens (dark and light), the evidence table, and a list of anything that needs the real supplier account to verify.

model DedicatedIp {
  id           String             @id @default(cuid())
  address      String             @unique
  ovhBlock     String // the OVH IP block/route this belongs to. Only meaningful for an OVH-provider node's rows; unused (kept "") for Hetzner rows.
  virtualMac   String?
  status       DedicatedIpStatus  @default(FREE)
  serverId     String?            @unique
  server       Server?            @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  // Which physical node's pool this IP belongs to — determines which
  // provider branch (OVH vs Hetzner) lib/dedicated-ip.ts uses to
  // allocate/release it. Every row has one; see Node.provider for the
  // per-provider dispatch this enables.
  nodeId       String
  node         Node               @relation(fields: [nodeId], references: [id])
  reverse      String?
  purpose      DedicatedIpPurpose @default(CUSTOMER)
  // Human label shown in place of a customer hostname for INTERNAL rows, e.g.
  // "Cold Email Relay". Not used for CUSTOMER rows (they show the Server hostname).
  purposeLabel String?
  createdAt    DateTime           @default(now())
}
model DedicatedCatalogItem {
  id                   String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// Upstream subsidiary the prices are for (e.g. "WE").
  subsidiary           String
  /// eco | baremetalServers (which public catalogue the plan came from).
  catalog              String
  /// Upstream plan code (ADMIN-ONLY). Regional variants are separate plans.
  planCode             String
  productCode          String
  /// kimsufi | soyoustart | rise | advance | game | scale | hgr | other
  range                String
  /// Upstream commercial name (ADMIN-ONLY, e.g. "ADVANCE-1").
  name                 String
  invoiceName          String
  cpuBrand             String
  cpuModel             String
  cpuCount             Int      @default(1)
  cpuCores             Int
  cpuThreads           Int
  cpuFrequencyGhz      Float?
  cpuBoostGhz          Float?
  defaultRamGb         Int?
  defaultStorage       String?
  defaultBandwidthMbps Int?
  /// Upstream datacenter codes this plan can be ordered in.
  datacenters          String[]
  currency             String
  /// Upstream monthly price (no commitment) + list setup fee, in cents.
  monthlyCents         Int
  setupCents           Int
  /// Setup after a live upstream promotion, null when none.
  promoSetupCents      Int?
  /// [{mode, months, termCents, setupCents}] commitment terms.
  terms                Json
  promotions           Json
  releaseYear          Int?
  slaPercent           Float?
  antiDdos             String?
  spec                 Json
  /// sha256 of the parsed item, to count real changes per sync.
  hash                 String

  // ---- Nxeon controls (never overwritten by a sync) ----
  /// Shown in customer catalogue. Default hidden: the owner opts items in.
  visible              Boolean  @default(false)
  /// Admin pin for the customer "Most popular" tag (lib/dedicated/tags.ts). Additive, 2026-10-07.
  popularPinned        Boolean  @default(false)
  /// Nxeon customer-facing name ("Nx Metal 6"); blank = generated from specs.
  displayName          String   @default("")
  markupPercent        Float?
  markupFixedCents     Int?
  overrideMonthlyCents Int?
  /// pass | waived | custom ; null = global default.
  setupPolicy          String?
  setupCustomCents     Int?
  /// Nxeon region codes hidden for this item only.
  hiddenRegions        String[] @default([])
  adminNote            String   @default("")

  firstSeenAt          DateTime @default(now())
  lastSeenAt           DateTime @default(now())
  /// Set when the plan disappears upstream (kept for history/offers, never deleted).
  removedAt            DateTime?
  priceChangedAt       DateTime?
  previousMonthlyCents Int?
  updatedAt            DateTime @updatedAt
  options              DedicatedCatalogOption[]

  @@unique([subsidiary, planCode])
  @@index([range])
  @@index([visible, removedAt])
}
model DedicatedCatalogOption {
  id            String               @id @default(cuid())
  itemId        String
  item          DedicatedCatalogItem @relation(fields: [itemId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  /// memory | storage | system-storage | bandwidth | vrack | gpu
  family        String
  planCode      String
  /// Upstream product code — joins DedicatedAvailability.memory/storage.
  productCode   String
  label         String
  isDefault     Boolean              @default(false)
  mandatory     Boolean              @default(false)
  monthlyCents  Int
  setupCents    Int                  @default(0)
  ramGb         Int?
  storageGb     Int?
  bandwidthMbps Int?
  trafficTb     Float?
  spec          Json
  lastSeenAt    DateTime             @default(now())
  removedAt     DateTime?

  @@unique([itemId, planCode])
  @@index([family])
}
model DedicatedAvailability {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// API host group the feed came from ("ca" | "eu" | "us").
  feed          String
  planCode      String
  fqn           String
  memory        String?
  storage       String?
  systemStorage String?
  datacenter    String
  /// 1H-high | 1H-low | 24H | 72H | 240H | 480H | comingSoon | unavailable | unknown
  availability  String
  fetchedAt     DateTime

  @@unique([feed, fqn, datacenter])
  @@index([planCode])
}
model DedicatedCatalogSync {
  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// worker | admin | script
  trigger          String
  subsidiary       String
  /// RUNNING | OK | PARTIAL | FAILED
  status           String    @default("RUNNING")
  startedAt        DateTime  @default(now())
  finishedAt       DateTime?
  durationMs       Int?
  plansSeen        Int       @default(0)
  added            Int       @default(0)
  changed          Int       @default(0)
  removed          Int       @default(0)
  priceChanges     Int       @default(0)
  optionsSeen      Int       @default(0)
  availabilityRows Int       @default(0)
  /// Per-catalogue counts + ranges + datacenters seen, for the admin panel.
  summary          Json?
  warnings         Json?
  error            String?
  requestedById    String?

  @@index([startedAt])
}
model DedicatedServer {
  id                     String                @id @default(cuid())
  /// Customer account (FK-less, like Offer.userId).
  userId                 String
  /// Customer-facing label ("Production DB").
  label                  String
  hostname               String?
  catalogItemId          String?
  /// The custom offer this machine was sold through (feature/chat-offers), if any.
  offerId                String?
  // ---- Specs as sold (frozen; the catalogue can drift) ----
  cpu                    String
  cores                  Int                   @default(0)
  threads                Int                   @default(0)
  ramGb                  Int                   @default(0)
  storage                String                @default("")
  bandwidth              String                @default("")
  /// Nxeon region code (e.g. "sgp1"); customers see its customer label only.
  region                 String
  // ---- ADMIN-ONLY upstream identity ----
  /// Upstream datacenter code (e.g. "sgp").
  datacenter             String?
  /// Upstream service name (e.g. "ns1234567.ip-1-2-3.net"). Same meaning as
  /// Node.providerServerId, so lib/ovh-admin's readers can take it later.
  providerServiceName    String?
  /// What it costs us per month (admin margin view only).
  costMonthlyCents       Int?
  // ---- Network / OS ----
  ipv4                   String[]              @default([])
  ipv6                   String[]              @default([])
  os                     String?
  status                 DedicatedServerStatus @default(PENDING)
  // ---- Credentials (encrypted with lib/crypto-box; customer reveals) ----
  credentialsUser        String?
  credentialsEnc         String?
  credentialsDeliveredAt DateTime?
  // ---- Billing (manual renewals) ----
  renewalDate            DateTime?
  renewalMonthlyCents    Int?
  termMonths             Int                   @default(1)
  setupFeeCents          Int                   @default(0)
  /// Linked Invoice ids (FK-less).
  invoiceIds             String[]              @default([])
  // ---- Notes ----
  notes                  String                @default("")
  provisionedAt          DateTime?
  suspendedAt            DateTime?
  suspendReason          String?
  cancelledAt            DateTime?
  createdById            String?
  // ---- Online order (customer checkout, lib/dedicated/order.ts) ----
  /// Client idempotency key of the paid order that created this row (null = added by staff).
  orderKey               String?
  /// What the customer bought, frozen at checkout (build, options, OS, term, amounts). Staff fulfil from it.
  orderConfig            Json?
  createdAt              DateTime              @default(now())
  updatedAt              DateTime              @updatedAt
  events                 DedicatedServerEvent[]
  requests               DedicatedServerRequest[]
  jobs                   DedicatedJob[]
  ipOrders               DedicatedIpOrder[]
  /// Rescue-mode password, encrypted (lib/crypto-box). Only set when staff store
  /// one; key-based rescue (the customer's SSH key) needs none.
  rescueSecretEnc        String?
  /// Monthly cents of extra IPs attached (already included in renewalMonthlyCents).
  extraIpMonthlyCents    Int                   @default(0)

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([status])
  @@index([orderKey])

This is a big task, so I'm planning the approach: I need a pure tracking module that takes status and timestamp inputs along with availability data from the order, though I'm realizing I need to check whether the order config stores the raw stock code or just the public-facing stock value.

I'll derive steps (done/current/todo/delayed), progress percentage, ETA text, and delivery status from that input, plus factor in the latest HANDOVER job's progress for the OS install phase. Then I need a server-only loader that pulls the server record, its latest handover job, order timestamps, and historical completed servers to build realistic ETAs.

For ownership, I'm wary of overlapping with bm-ops' planned `tracking-data.ts` file — I'll keep my piece pure and write my own loader at `lib/dedicated/tracking-load.ts`, checking their worktree periodically to avoid duplicate work. I also need a gated, owner-checked server action for polling the tracking view every 25 seconds.

Now I'm shifting to the wizard UI redesign: a WizardHero component showing build name, size art, spec mini-cards, location flag, and a Configure/Review/Pay step indicator, keeping the "All builds" back button, then moving into the Configure step's location section.

The pricing summary needs to show each upgrade cost live, but I realize the per-option extra costs computed in isolation won't sum exactly to the combined price due to the markup/uplift rounding formula ending in .99 — so I need a way to itemize that still adds up correctly, perhaps by treating the base as the default variant price rather than summing isolated deltas.

Showing a single combined "Upgrades" line instead of per-option prices could work, but those are already displayed individually in the picker, so duplicating with different totals seems confusing. I'm also worried about rounding: with price-ending-in-99 rounding, the sum of individual option deltas can diverge from the true combined delta by up to roughly a dollar per option, which could explain an odd total like $156.99 when the base and listed extras don't quite add up.

I'm not confident guessing at the exact arithmetic here—this looks like a genuine pricing bug worth investigating with actual seeded data rather than speculation, since the default storage option's price delta might not be zero like I assumed.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)

With enough history, I'll compute median and p80 to say "ready within about N hours," capped at a minimum of 1 hour, and flag the step as delayed—with a reassuring note and support link—once elapsed time exceeds the promised window.

For cancellation, if there's no provisioning timestamp, I'll show progress up through payment and then mark the order ended with "This order was cancelled." I'm also defining a `TrackingFacts` type with an optional supplier phase field (ordered/delivering/delivered/installing/error) so the ops agent can populate it, mapping each phase to the right step and note—delivering to rack-and-connect, installing to setup, error to delayed. Now I'm working out the progress percentage as a piecewise interpolation across received, paid, and setup stages.

I decide against pure time-based interpolation since it risks overstating progress — instead I'll base percentage on completed steps plus partial credit for install progress, and show elapsed-vs-expected time as separate text labeled "Estimated." I'm mapping out which fields the loader can pull directly from the database — order timestamps, provisioning event times, the latest handover job status, delivery as provisioning completion, and stock availability captured at order time.

Since raw stock codes aren't stored today, I'm considering adding a `stockCode`/`availabilityCode` field to InternalQuote or orderConfig so future orders capture the actual availability tier, with a fallback that maps the existing public stock labels ("1H-high", "1H-low", "24H") into a rough in-stock/limited bucket defaulting to a 24-hour window when unspecified. For historical duration data, I'm defining "completed" orders as those with both an orderKey and a provisionedAt, computing duration as provisionedAt minus createdAt across up to 200 records from the last 180 days.

I'm requiring at least 3 samples before trusting the data, preferring region-specific stats when that threshold is met but falling back to global averages otherwise. When history exists, I'll use the p75 duration rounded to a friendly unit for the ETA message; when it doesn't, I'll derive wording from the availability code itself, tying it to our actual stated promises rather than inventing numbers — codes at or under 24H map to "usually ready within 24 hours," 72H to "within 3 days," and 240H to "within 10 days," since those reflect real business commitments rather than fabricated install-time assumptions.

For delayed orders, I'm flagging anything where elapsed time exceeds the max of 24 hours or the code's window and hasn't delivered yet, plus treating a failed handover job as an automatic delay trigger with a reassuring message that the team's been alerted. I also want to model an optional supplier phase field in the tracking facts — ordered, delivering, delivered, or error — so step three can show "being racked, cabled and tested" during delivery and mark itself done once hardware arrives. Each completed step should carry a timestamp, and the current step should show how long it's been active. Now I'm writing the tracking.ts file itself.

I'm working through step navigation using URL hash state, pushing history entries for each step so browser back/forward works, and handling popstate to restore the right step when the hash matches this build. Comparing the pre-tax net total (term + setup) from the fresh quote against what was shown at Continue-press time — if they differ, I show a notice explaining the total changed due to pricing or stock updates since the page loaded. For the pay step, I'm defining method eligibility: wallet covers full total, split requires partial spendable balance, and the server enforces the same spendable logic. Card sessions open when entering pay with card/split, but since payDedicatedOrder now requires the no-refund acknowledgment to be ticked (already gated at Review), unticking it on the Pay step should disable Deploy even though the session was already created.

I also want to keep "Signed in as {email}" on the pay step, and redesign the Review content with a cleaner spec list, a compact "After you deploy" section with an honest ETA, and the no-refund notice.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

[ $# -gt 0 ] || die "usage: devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD..."
    [ "$lock" = 1 ] && [ -z "$max" ] && max=1500   # keep the shared lock bounded (release builds wait max 30 min)
    prepare
    run_remote "$lock" "$max" "$@" ;;

  tsc)   prepare; run_remote 0 1800 npx tsc --noEmit "$@" ;;
  test)  prepare; if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then run_remote 1 1500 npx tsx --test "$@"; else run_remote 1 1500 bash -c 'npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts'; fi ;;
  build) prepare; run_remote 1 1500 npx next build "$@" ;;

  dev|bg)
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then bname=dev; else bname="${1:?usage: devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...}"; shift; fi
    case "$bname" in *[!a-z0-9-]*) die "bad name $bname" ;; esac
    init_ws; port="$PORT"
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --port) port="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then set -- npx next dev -H 127.0.0.1 -p "$port"; fi
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "no command"
    ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0
    unit="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$bname"
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$unit") 2>/dev/null; $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --bg --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "$unit" -- env PORT="$port" "$@")" </dev/null >/dev/null
    say "started $unit on node-2 (127.0.0.1:$port only). Logs: scripts/devhost logs $bname -f"
    say "reach it from the primary:  scripts/devhost tunnel $port   (then http://127.0.0.1:$port)"
    say "or test it ON node-2:        scripts/devhost run -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
    say "stop it when done:           scripts/devhost stop $bname" ;;

  stop)
    init_ws; which="${1:-all}"
    if [ "$which" = all ]; then
      bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; echo \"stopped \$u\"; done" </dev/null
    else
      bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") && echo stopped nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which" </dev/null
    fi ;;

  logs)
    init_ws; which=dev; [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "${1:0:1}" != - ] && { which="$1"; shift; }
    bh_ssh "journalctl --no-pager -o cat -u $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") $(q "${@:--n100}")" ;;

  tunnel)
    rport="${1:?usage: devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]}"; lport="${2:-$rport}"
    say "forwarding primary 127.0.0.1:$lport -> node-2 127.0.0.1:$rport (Ctrl-C to close)"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    exec ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L "127.0.0.1:$lport:127.0.0.1:$rport" "$BUILD_HOST" ;;

  pull)
    init_ws; src="${1:?usage: devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]}"; dst="${2:-.}"
    case "$src" in /*|*..*) die "path must be relative to the workspace" ;; esac
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    rsync -a --compress -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/$src" "$dst" ;;

  db)
    init_ws; ensure_remote
    case "${1:-info}" in
      push)  push_files; deps 0; run_remote 0 900 npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate ;;
      reset) bh_ssh ". /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env; export PGPASSWORD=\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD; dropdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U \$AGENT_PGUSER --if-exists --force $DBNAME && createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U \$AGENT_PGUSER $DBNAME && echo recreated $DBNAME" </dev/null
             say "now: scripts/devhost db push" ;;
      info)  echo "throwaway database $DBNAME on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433 (role nxeon_agent); DATABASE_URL is preset for every devhost command" ;;
      *) die "usage: devhost db push|reset|info" ;;
    esac ;;

  env)
    init_ws; ensure_remote
    case "${1:-list}" in
      list) bh_ssh "sed -E 's/^([A-Z0-9_]*(SECRET|PASSWORD|TOKEN|KEY|URL)[A-Z0-9_]*)=.*/\1=<set>/' $(q "$ENVF")" </dev/null ;;
      set)
        kv="${2:?usage: devhost env set KEY=VALUE}"; k="${kv%%=*}"; v="${kv#*=}"
        case "$k" in ""|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) die "bad key $k" ;; DATABASE_URL) die "DATABASE_URL is fixed to the throwaway DB" ;; esac
        # Refuse anything that is a live production value (compared here, never printed).
        for f in /opt/nxeon/.env /opt/nxeon-staging/.env; do
          [ -r "$f" ] && [ ${#v} -ge 12 ] && cut -d= -f2- "$f" | tr -d '"'"'" | grep -qxF -- "$v" && die "refusing: that value is a live value from $f. devhost never gets production/staging credentials."
        done

Lines are telescoping differences of the server's exact price table (`OrderVariant.allPrices`, every memory x storage x bandwidth combo, plus `baseMonthlyCents` and `defaults`, computed in `buildOne` by the same `sellFor` the charge uses), so they add up to the charged monthly price to the cent; each option tile shows the same marginal figure. Review's "Continue to payment" uses the same button.
- **Choices survive going back**: `BareMetalFlow` keeps each build's choices (and its order key) for the visit, so All builds -> reopen restores them; the step is mirrored in the hash (`#build=…&step=review`, replaceState) and a refresh on Review/Pay returns to Review.

- `raw.expectedTotalCents` (the total on screen): a fresh quote that differs is refused with "The price changed to $X (from $Y)… Nothing was charged", so neither the wallet nor the card path can charge a total the customer did not see.

Promotional credit is estimated conservatively (every grant assumed unspent, capped at the balance): signup credit, top-up promo-code bonuses, riddle awards, referral welcome rewards. The quote returns `balanceCents`, `spendableCents`, `promoCents`. The card-leg fulfilment (`placeDedicatedOrder` debiting the stamped total) does not re-check promo credit; that is bm-ops' server-side rule.
'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor, anchor+add,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
echo ok

Overall it looks decent—the hero art renders fine though a bit small, the account balance display is partially obscured by the dev badge, and I'm noticing something to check about the Canada location field.

The base build price adds up correctly with the memory upgrade, though the "Included" label on an out-of-stock option is a minor inconsistency. Let me check the other screenshots too.
The memory spec and balance display look fine overall, just some minor redundancy that I can overlook. Moving on to complete the payment with the card.

Without Stripe keys in dev, the card step should show an error, so the hint text needs to change to point at that message instead of the generic "fill in your card details" line. I'm also noticing the hero animation looks dimmer when switching to the pay step, likely because the component isn't remounting and the entrance animation is being caught mid-way through.

I'm checking that the "last 6 bare metal orders" count correctly includes the delivered seed order, and reviewing the lit/dim progress visual at 74% to make sure the dim region is still visible. I also notice the setup step's completion timestamp wraps to a second line due to label length, which seems fine for the layout.

The step time for setup done pulls from the instance's startedAt field, which looks correct. Now I should double-check the delayed and queued states.

The dim/lit effect is working well at 15% lit. For delayed orders, I should hide the "Expected by" text since it's showing a past date — that doesn't make sense when something's delayed. I should also check the eta basis text and consider adding a help link for delayed orders, referencing the Frankfurt data center context in that message.

Now I'm reviewing the queued, delivered, and services states.

I'm noticing the ServiceCard preview actually uses the stock image rather than a custom size render, with the rack art swapped to the baremetal asset. I'm also checking the mini step tracker on the card.

For the card's status labels I need shorter text, like "Setting up in our ${loc} data center", "Installing your operating system", and "Taking a little longer than usual" for delayed. For the delayed state I also want to swap the ETA text to "Our team is on it" instead of the usual 6-hour estimate, fixing this in services-rows. After the card chip is sorted, I'll move on to the wallet pay and promo screenshots.

I notice the wallet payment summary duplicates info—showing both "From wallet" and "From your balance" with the same amount. I should simplify so wallet-only payments show just the total "Paid from your balance" line without redundant rows, while split payments keep the "From wallet" row plus a "Charged to card" total. Let me check the 32-after-wallet-pay state next.

The wallet deduction confirms correctly: $63.09 debited, leaving 9,936.91. I should fix the awkward "since your order" wording to say "Ordered just now" when elapsed time is zero, and hide "Expected by" when status is "Delayed".

Beyond that, I need to shorten the step labels in services-rows cards, adjust delayed ETA text, remove wallet duplication in the pay summary, and add a hint on DeployButton when payError occurs. After these fixes, I'll do a pass for light mode and mobile responsiveness.

input.message:
**bm-wizard: done.** Branch `feature/bm-wizard` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/bm-wizard`), 2 commits (`ae175ff06e`, `0669967df5`). Not merged, not deployed. No live supplier calls, no real money: the catalogue came from the recorded test fixtures, payments ran on the throwaway node-2 DB, and the dev server is stopped. The final `tsc` under the lock is clean, and 33/33 tests pass across tracking, price-lines, brand-voice and order.

**What was built**
1. **Hero** (`components/dedicated/flow/WizardHero.tsx`): always dark, with the build's size render on the aurora plate, family and tags, name, the CPU/GPU logos, the chosen location with its flag, and spec mini-cards that change as the customer picks options. It has a Configure / Review / Pay step indicator.
2. **Configure, review and pay fixes** (`Configurator.tsx`)
   - **Price summary bug fixed.** Option tiles used to price each option on its own against the defaults, so with the $X.99 rounding they didn't add up to the total. The new summary is built from the server's full price table (`lib/dedicated/price-lines.ts`, with tests) and adds up to the cent: base, each upgrade, monthly, first month or 12×, setup fee, Due today, renewal.
   - A price that changes between Configure and Review is now called out, not silent. The pay action also refuses a total different from the one on screen (`expectedTotalCents`).
   - Auto-switching memory/storage to an in-stock partner now shows a note.
   - Choices are kept when going back to the catalogue and reopening the build.
   - Choices are proper radio buttons for keyboard and screen readers.
   - On phones a bottom bar keeps the total and the next button in reach.
3. **Classic deploy button:** `btn-deploy` "Deploy server →" with disabled (with a hint saying why), "Deploying…" and done states, plus a double-click guard.
4. **No refunds, no discounts:** the notice and a required acknowledgement checkbox appear on Review and Pay. The server refuses to pay without `acceptedNoRefund: true`. The flow had no coupon or money-back text to remove.
5. **Spendable wallet only** (your later instruction): the Pay step uses only real funds and shows "Promotional credit can't be used for dedicated servers" with the split. The card path is never blocked by the wallet.
6. **Order tracker**
   - `lib/dedicated/tracking.ts` holds the pure logic, with 14 tests.
   - `tracking-load.ts` reads only our own records, never the supplier.
   - On the server page, `OrderTracker.tsx` shows the size render powering up to the real progress (it stays still under reduced motion), the five steps with times, "our {Montreal} data center", and the ETA. It refreshes from our records every 25 s and shows "Last updated". It keeps the last good state if a refresh fails, and offers "Open your server" once delivered.
   - The ETA comes from the 75th percentile of past delivery times when there are at least 3, otherwise the stock code at order time, otherwise our 24-hour promise.
   - My Services cards show a compact tracker.
   - Orders now record the raw stock code at checkout.

**What I ran**
- Playwright against the real routes, dark and light, 1440 and 390, through configure → review → pay, plus the queued / installing / delayed / delivered tracker states and My Services.
- **Wallet payment exercised end to end on the throwaway DB:** $63.09 was debited, the PAID invoice and the PENDING server were created, and the page landed on the tracker.
- The promo-credit account showed the note and the correct split.
- **The card path was only checked up to its "card payments aren't available" error.** I didn't copy a Stripe test key to node-2, because the rules forbid moving secrets there, so a Stripe test-mode card payment was not run.
- Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/bm-release/wizard/shots/`. Notes and resume steps: `/root/agent-notes/bm-release/wizard/NOTES.md`. Docs: new section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

**Contract for bm-ops (not merged)**
- The pay payload carries `acceptedNoRefund: true` and `expectedTotalCents`. Recording `acceptedNoRefundAt` and putting it in the card leg's Stripe metadata is still theirs to do.
- `lib/dedicated/wallet-view.ts` (`dedicatedWallet()` → `{balanceCents, spendableCents, promoCents}`) is a stand-in. It treats every promo grant ever received (signup credit, top-up bonuses, riddle award, referral bonus) as still unspent, which is conservative. bm-ops should replace it with their helper.
- Card-leg fulfilment does not re-check promo credit; that server-side rule is theirs.
- They can fill `supplierPhase` in `tracking-load.ts` (`factsFor`) once they cache the supplier's delivery task.

**Issues to know about**
- `test/dedicated-gate.test.ts` fails 2 tests on import (`createContext is not a function`). I didn't touch `gate.ts`, so it's probably the node-2 test setup, but I didn't confirm that on `main`.
- The 390 px pages logged a hydration attribute-mismatch warning. I didn't find its source.
- The IP order status "Refunded" (an extra-IP order rejected before purchase) is in bm-ops' area.
- My first dev server overlapped another agent's for about a minute before I stopped it. A later one was killed when the node-2 agent memory cap ran out, and was restarted once.

**For the owner to decide:** whether the ETA should stay anchored to the 24-hour promise even for 1-hour stock codes (currently it does, so we never promise "1 hour" while staff still build by hand).
